title: COPE COPD – A Feasibility Study of the Implementation and Adaptation of an Outpatient Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Aftercare Program Following Inpatient Pulmonary Treatment
summary:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a chronic lung disease that makes breathing difficult and may worsen over time. Many people with COPD experience not only physical symptoms but also psychological distress, such as anxiety, depressed mood, or feelings of uncertainty. These emotional difficulties can make it harder to cope with the disease and may have an additional negative impact on health and quality of life.

Following a hospital stay due to an acute worsening of COPD, many patients feel particularly vulnerable and worry about experiencing another exacerbation. During this period, additional psychological support may help patients better manage their daily lives and cope with their condition.

This study aims to determine whether a new specialized psychotherapeutic follow-up program (COPE COPD) can be successfully integrated into routine care at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin. In addition, the study will investigate how participants evaluate the program and whether there are initial indications of improvements in psychological well-being and coping with COPD.

The program is based on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and is designed to help participants better manage psychological distress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms while improving their overall quality of life.
conditions: Psychiatric comorbidities and subclinical psychological symptoms in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation, unspecified
Psychological and behavioural factors associated with disorders or diseases classified elsewhere

interventions.name:
A manualized, diagnosis-specific cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) intervention (8 weekly sessions of 60 minutes each over 8-10 weeks; 10 participants) for psychological aftercare following inpatient treatment for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
- Current inpatient treatment (typically due to an acute exacerbation) at the Department of Pulmonology, respiratory medicine and intensive care of Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin
- Sufficient cognitive and language abilities to participate in the sessions and complete the study questionnaires
- Ability to participate in the planned online sessions (technical requirements may be established with support, if necessary)
- Written informed consent obtained prior to study participation
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute suicidality or an acute risk of harm to self or others
- Acute psychotic symptoms or severe psychiatric disorders requiring more intensive treatment
- Severe cognitive impairment that precludes participation in the intervention, or a medical condition that prevents participation in the sessions or the intervention
